$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the General section's Agent Chat defaults for new chats (cx-d5b5d). scripts/cmux-next/gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptors and parser constants from it (its docstring is the row format); schemas/settings/settings-schema.json is still exported from Swift and must not change when rows move here.

lists.name: agentDefaults
lists.note: The defaults a new agent chat starts with (Agents > Agent Chat).

rows.name: permissionMode
rows.note: acpmux reads it at each new chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/hub/start_mode.rs): a mode picked in a chat applies to that chat only (Leo 2026-10-21). A value MDM or the team policy forces reaches acpmux through the app's settings push (ChatSettings) and wins over the settings file.

help.text: What a new chat may do without asking. A mode you pick in a chat applies to that chat only.

rows.note: How long Claude Code keeps a chat's prompt cached. acpmux reads it at each Claude Code start (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/prompt_cache_env.rs).

help.text: One hour keeps replies after a pause cheap; its cache writes cost a little more.

rows.name: agentEnv
rows.note: Variables every agent chat gets, as Claude Code's env setting and Codex's shell_environment_policy.set. acpmux reads it at each chat start (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/agent_env.rs): a value the profile, preset, route, session or login shell sets wins; a remote-origin chat gets none.

help.text: Variables every new chat's agent and its tools get. A value an agent profile already sets wins.

rows.name: agentEnvExclude
rows.note: Variable names (or PREFIX_*) no agent chat gets, as Codex's shell_environment_policy.exclude. acpmux removes them last when it builds the agent's command (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/agent_env.rs); its own ACPMUX_* session wiring stays.

help.text: Variable names agents never get, such as AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_*.

rows.name: additionalDirectories
rows.note: Folders every new chat gets on top of its Sources, as Claude Code's additionalDirectories setting: Claude Code --add-dir, ACP additionalDirectories. acpmux adds them at chat creation (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/hub/additional_dirs.rs); a folder that is not there is skipped; a remote-origin chat gets none.

help.text: Added to every new chat's Sources. Use full or ~/ paths.

rows.name: sandboxMode
rows.note: acpmux reads it at each new chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/agent_sandbox.rs). permissionMode (default, what acpmux did before): the sandbox follows the permission mode; the Codex bridge's modes carry their own sandbox_mode (ask and agent workspace-write, read-only read-only, agent-full-access danger-full-access) and Claude Code runs without its sandbox. workspaceWrite: full-access modes are off, as with sessions.allowFullAccess off, so Codex never runs danger-full-access; Claude Code starts with --settings sandbox.enabled true and sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands false, merged into the launch's own inline --settings (its sandbox covers Bash). A remote-origin chat keeps its own sandbox.

help.text: Workspace Only keeps agents' writes inside their workspace and turns full-access modes off.

rows.name: sandboxNetwork
rows.note: acpmux reads it at each new chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/agent_sandbox.rs). harness (default, what acpmux did before): each harness's own; Codex's workspace-write sandbox has no network, Claude Code's sandbox asks per domain. allow: the codex app-server launch gets -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true unless its command line or codex's config sets that key; a mode switched to mid-chat uses the bridge's own policy, which has no network. Claude Code's network rules stay its own. A remote-origin chat keeps its own.

help.text: Allow lets Codex's workspace sandbox reach the network.

rows.name: modelRouterModel
rows.note: The model the cmux model router profile (cmux) starts new chats on; acpmux reads it when it builds that profile (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/config/discover.rs add_cmux_router). The choices are the router's DeepSeek models, default first (user 2026-10-28: DeepSeek only, the 10/17 build with images by default); CMUX_ROUTER_MODELS in acpmux and the backend allowlist (INFERENCE_MODEL_ALLOWLIST) hold the same list.

help.text: The model new cmux model router chats start on.

rows.name: claudeDefaultModel
rows.note: The model a new Claude Code chat starts on when the chat names none. acpmux reads it at each new chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/model_settings.rs, hub/start_defaults.rs): above config.json defaults (a pick in a chat), below a per-chat pick, a preset, a folder profile or a profile's own model. Empty: today's chain (the last pick, the CLI's own config, the catalog default).

title.text: Claude Code Model for New Chats

help.text: A model id such as claude-opus-5-5. Empty starts on the last model you picked.

rows.name: claudeDefaultEffort
rows.note: The reasoning effort a new Claude Code chat starts on when the chat names none; acpmux reads it at each new chat (model_settings.rs, hub/start_defaults.rs), in the same order as the model row. An effort the starting model lacks is skipped. auto: today's chain.

title.text: Claude Code Effort for New Chats

help.text: How hard a new chat thinks. Last Used keeps the last effort you picked.

rows.name: codexDefaultModel
rows.note: The model a new Codex chat starts on when the chat names none. acpmux reads it at each new chat (cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/model_settings.rs, hub/start_defaults.rs): above config.json defaults (a pick in a chat), below a per-chat pick, a preset, a folder profile or a profile's own model. Empty: today's chain (the last pick, the CLI's own config, the catalog default).

help.text: A model id such as gpt-6.2-sol. Empty starts on the last model you picked.

rows.name: codexDefaultEffort
rows.note: The reasoning effort a new Codex chat starts on when the chat names none; acpmux reads it at each new chat (model_settings.rs, hub/start_defaults.rs), in the same order as the model row. An effort the starting model lacks is skipped. auto: today's chain.

help.text: How hard a new chat thinks. Last Used keeps the last effort you picked.

rows.name: textGenerationModel
rows.note: The Claude model that writes cmux's generated text: chat titles, task names, rolling summaries and diff hunk summaries (every _acpmux/complete that names no model and runs on Claude Code, cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/hub/complete.rs and hub/titles.rs, read through model_settings.rs). acpmux config titles.model / summaries.model still win. cmux NEXT writes no commit messages or PR text with a model. Default haiku, the small model these ran on before the row.

help.text: The Claude model that writes chat titles and summaries.

lists.name: agentTools
lists.note: Settings > Agents > cmux Tools: the onboarding step's question (do agents the person starts in cmux, its terminals and agent chats, get cmux's MCP server?) and its answer, beside the card that lists the agents on this Mac, an old cmux entry in one's own config (with Remove) and the manual lines for agents started elsewhere.

rows.name: cmuxMcp
rows.note: Whether agents cmux starts get its cmux MCP server (cmux mcp serve, which carries cmux Computer Use): a Claude Code or Codex typed into a cmux terminal (the claude and codex shims, cmux-tui agent_mcp_choice.rs) and the app's agent chats (acpmux agent_tools.rs agents_get_cmux), all with one server definition named cmux (acpmux agent_tools::cmux_server) and the app's settings file. Only through the launch: cmux never writes an agent's own config; cmux setup mcp reports which agents get it and the manual lines a person runs to use it elsewhere. ask (unset) is no answer yet: no server, and the app asks at launch (OnboardingWindowPresenter.askAgentToolsOnce); on is the person's yes (it also turns the server on for these agents unless mcp.enabled says otherwise, cli/mcp/config.rs); off gives none. A Chief turn keeps its own cmux tool list either way. Rust reads it with cmux_tui_core::user_settings::AgentsCmuxMcp.

title.text: cmux Tools for Agents in cmux

help.text: Agents you start in cmux get cmux’s tools, Computer Use included: Claude Code and Codex in cmux’s terminals and agent chats. Until you choose, they get nothing. cmux never changes your agents’ own settings.

summary.text: Whether agents you start in cmux get cmux’s tools
